summary: Obfuscated daemon accepts remote commands from a configurable gateway over WebSocket
details: The package ships a `whalent` daemon (bin entry and main = dist/index.cjs) that connects outbound to a WebSocket gateway (`--gateway wss://...` or WHALENT_GATEWAY_INSTANCE_ID) and, per its own README, accepts remote commands including upgrade and restart from that gateway. Runtime dependencies are the standard remote-terminal stack: `ws`, `node-pty`, `@xterm/headless`, and `ssh2`; the bundled dist/core.cjs references `process.env.SHELL` and loopback RDP/VNC ports 127.0.0.1:3389/5900/5901, consistent with PTY spawning and remote-desktop bridging on the host running the daemon. Both entrypoints (dist/index.cjs, 112 KB; dist/core.cjs, 13.6 MB) are shipped as heavy javascript-obfuscator output with rotated string arrays, hex-numbered identifiers (_0xNNNN), and control-flow flattening; the package's own devDependencies include `javascript-obfuscator` and a `build:fast` script that toggles it off, confirming the shipped artifacts are the obfuscated build. The combination means a remote party at the configured gateway can drive shell/PTY execution on the installer's host, and the obfuscated runtime prevents inspection of the actual command surface exposed to that gateway (whether it is limited to `upgrade`/`restart` as advertised, or extends to arbitrary shell).

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
